item.title: Salt, Voltage, and the Silent Anion Gate: Endocrine Hypertension & Anion-Exchanger Channelopathies (KCNJ5, CLCN2, CACNA1D, Pendred & Congenital Chloride Diarrhea) — One-Ångström walks inside GIRK2/KCNJ5 (4KFM), human ClC-2 + AK-42 (8GQU), CaV1.3 EEEE/Gly403 (7UHG), and Pendrin (7WL7); adrenal GHK depolarization & ARR/AVS physics; mutant-selective macrolides, ABE9/PEmax & SLC26A4 ASO blueprints; and the USD 1.8 billion aldosterone synthase biotech saga (osilodrostat, baxdrostat, lorundrostat)
item.description: Wave 11 Channelopathies Episode CHAN_15 (Ep 2681): Five-act One-Ångström-Tall Man medical, biophysical, base-editing, and biotech-history treatise covering endocrine hypertension channelopathies (KCNJ5/GIRK4 FH-III vs. somatic APA & G151E cell-death paradox; CLCN2 GoF FH-II vs. recessive CC2L leukoencephalopathy/chorioretinopathy/azoospermia; CACNA1D GoF PASNA vs. recessive exon-8B SANDD at Gly403) and sister SLC26 epithelial anion exchangers (SLC26A4 Pendred syndrome EVA/goiter/perchlorate discharge & SLC26A3 Congenital Chloride Diarrhea fecal Cl- > 90 mM with metabolic alkalosis). Anchored to verified RCSB PDB geometries 4KFM, 8GQU, 7UHG, and 7WL7; includes two spoken calculation pauses (zona glomerulosa GHK depolarization shifts; ARR/AVS lateralization, CLD stool Cl- flux, and empirical Phase 3 BaxHTN/Launch-HTN BP reductions); covers mutant-selective macrolides (MAPA), AK-42, codon-exact ABE9/PEmax/SLC26A4 c.919-2A>G ASO strategies, and the 20-year CYP11B2 vs. CYP11B1 ASI biotech history (Novartis/Recordati USD 390 million osilodrostat, CinCor/AstraZeneca USD 1.8 billion baxdrostat, Mineralys USD 192 million IPO lorundrostat).

item.title: Cilia, Slit Diaphragms, and Acidic Endosomes: PKD2 ADPKD, TRPC6 Podocyte FSGS & CLCN5 Dent Disease 1 — Mayo htTKV & PKD1 6-pseudogene traps, steroid-resistant TRPC6 FSGS & the calcineurin-synaptopodin paradox, Dent 1 CLCN5 vs. OCRL LMW proteinuria, 1-Å cryo-EM walks inside PKD2 (5T4D), TRPC6+AM-0883 (6UZ8) & CLC-7/OSTM1 (7JM7, Glu247=ClC-5 Glu211), endosomal V-ATPase stall & TEMPO/REPRISE economics, Otsuka Jynarque REMS, Novartis USD 1.7B Regulus farabursen buyout, Boehringer BI 764198 Lancet FSGS readout, and base/prime/CRISPRa editing across the glomerular filtration barrier
item.description: Wave 11 Channelopathies Episode CHAN_16 (Ep 2682): Five-act One-Ångström-Tall Man medical, structural-biophysics, gene-editing, and biotech-history treatise uniting three specialized renal subcellular microdomains: (1) Primary-cilium PKD2 (TRPP2) / PKD1 ADPKD (Mayo Imaging Classification 1A-1E, 8-11% intracranial berry aneurysm MRA screening, PKD1 exons 1-33 6-pseudogene LR-PCR trap, Cornec-Le Gall median ESRD ages 55.6/67.9/79.7 yr, Outeda 2026 D511V VSD destabilization & Tian 2026 RASSF4 potentiation); (2) Podocyte slit-diaphragm dominant GoF TRPC6 FSGS (P112Q, M132T, R895C, E897K; steroid resistance & calcineurin-synaptopodin-cathepsin-L paradox; up to 14% monogenic adult FSGS); and (3) Proximal-tubule apical endosomal CLCN5 Dent Disease 1 vs. OCRL Dent Disease 2 (dipstick-albumin discordance, 100x-1000x urine beta-2-microglobulin/RBP, hypercalciuria, medullary nephrocalcinosis, rickets, 30-80% ESRD ages 30-50). Grounded in three verified RCSB PDB cryo-EM structures with 40+ measured interatomic distances: 5T4D (3.0 Å human PKD2 nanodisc: LGD selectivity filter Asp643-Arg638 2.67 Å, Gly642-Ile639 2.91 Å, S6 Leu677 hydrophobic gate 3.41 Å), 6UZ8 (2.84 Å human TRPC6 + agonist AM-0883 R0D + lipid SBM: FSGS brake contacts Arg895-Glu897 2.91 Å, Met132-Lys864 2.92 Å, Pro112-Glu900 3.47 Å, R0D-Trp680 3.32 Å, R0D-SBM lipid kiss 3.72 Å), and 7JM7 (2.82 Å human CLC-7/OSTM1 homolog of ClC-5: gating glutamate Glu247 [= ClC-5 Glu211] 2.98 Å from S_ext CL904, S_cen CL903-Tyr602 2.29 Å, S_int CL905-Gly203 2.77 Å, CBS ATP-Lys785 1.69 Å, ATP-Mg 1.96 Å, Mg-Glu95 2.43 Å, interfacial PI(3)P 0J1-Lys285 2.17 Å). Includes two fully worked spoken Calculation Pauses (300-nm endosome V-ATPase 318-ms stall at 3,177 H+ / +180 mV vs. 357,571 H+ buffered requirement and ClC-5 +42.0 mM luminal Cl- concentration; Mayo Class 1D htTKV doubling times & REPRISE 6.77 dialysis-free years vs. USD 280,000/yr Jynarque economics), full biotech histories (Otsuka tolvaptan TEMPO 3:4 / 2013 CRL / REPRISE / 2018 REMS; Regulus RGLS4326 clinical hold -> farabursen RGLS8429 Phase 1b 0.05% htTKV arrest -> Novartis 2025 USD 800M upfront / USD 1.7B CVR acquisition; Vertex VX-407 AGLOW; Boehringer Ingelheim BI 764198 COVID-19 ARDS Thorax 2023 failure -> Lancet 2026 FSGS 35% vs 7.1% / 44% at 20 mg & Phase 3 NCT07220083), ABE8e/CBE/iSTOP/Prime/CRISPRa strategies across the 6-8 nm glomerular filtration barrier, textbook myth debunking (Delling & Clapham 2016 cilia Ca2+, immune-FSGS dogma, Jentsch 2010 ClC-5 E211A uncoupling), and a decisive two-arm cryo-EM + porcine/NHP renal-delivery experiment.

item.title: The Upside-Down Metronome and the Stalled Wire: HCN1 DEE, HCN4 Familial Sick Sinus & IST, and TRPM4 Progressive Heart Block — SCN1A-Negative Dravet-Mimic HCN1 Cation-Leak DEE (M305L, G391D, D401H), HCN4 LoF Bradycardia/LVNC/AFib vs. R524Q Inappropriate Sinus Tachycardia, TRPM4 E7K Impaired-DeSUMOylation Purkinje Depolarization Block, One-Ångström Walks Inside 5U6P/7NP4/6BQV, Phase-4 SA-Node & GHK Interneuron Calculations, Servier/Amgen Ivabradine (SHIFT vs. SIGNIFY & Phosphenes), Propofol-Site Stabilizers, ABE9/Prime Editing, and HCN2/TBX18 Biological Pacemakers
item.description: Wave 11 Channelopathies Episode CHAN_17 (Ep 2683): Five-act One-Ångström-Tall Man medical, structural, and biotech treatise uniting three pacemaker and conduction channelopathies: (1) de novo HCN1 transmembrane cation-leak DEE (M305L, G391D, D401H) mimicking SCN1A Dravet syndrome with febrile status epilepticus and paradoxical phenytoin/lamotrigine exacerbation; (2) HCN4 bi-directional cardiac pacemaker disease contrasting autosomal-dominant LoF familial sinus bradycardia (34-42 bpm), LVNC, atrial fibrillation, and AV block against C-linker GoF R524Q cAMP-hypersensitive familial Inappropriate Sinus Tachycardia; and (3) TRPM4 E7K (c.19G>A) autosomal-dominant Progressive Familial Heart Block Type IB (PFHB1B), where impaired deSUMOylation/endocytosis stacks 2-3x excess monovalent Na+-conducting TRPM4 channels on His-Purkinje fibers, depolarizing V_rest and driving NaV1.5 into steady-state inactivation (conduction block). Anchored at 1 Å inside three verified RCSB cryo-EM PDBs: 5U6P (3.51 Å human HCN1 + cAMP: S4 Arg267-Asn179 2.99 Å / Asp233 3.77 Å, flared CIGYG Cys358 3.09/3.26 Å vs. Tyr361 14.22 Å, S5 Met305-S6 Phe389 4.78 Å propofol/M305L clutch, S6 Val390 gate 3.62/3.79 Å, CNBD Arg549-cAMP 2.76 Å), 7NP4 (3.3 Å cAMP-bound rabbit HCN4 with explicit +1 residue mapping to human HCN4: CIGYG Ile480-Ser475 2.87 Å, outward S6 Phe510-Tyr507 3.12 Å / Met426 4.13 Å bracing the open-pore ivabradine cavity, CNBD Cys663-cAMP 2.54 Å and Arg670-cAMP 2.87 Å), and 6BQV (3.1 Å human TRPM4 + Ca2+ nanodisc: monovalent FGQIPQED filter Gln977 7.21 Å / Glu981 10.68 Å excluding Ca2+, Ile1040 3.72 Å & Tyr1045 S6 lower gate, S1-S4 Ca2+ pocket Gln831 2.27 Å and Glu828/Asn865/Asp868 2.66 Å). Includes two verified spoken calculation pauses (SA-node Phase-4 slope dV/dt = -I_net/C_m showing 70 -> 42 and 115 bpm balanced-current amplification; mixed Na+/K+ GHK E_rev at P_Na/P_K = 0.25 vs. 1.0 driving cortical PV+ interneuron NaV1.1 depolarization block), full Servier/Amgen ivabradine business & SHIFT (N=6,558) vs. SIGNIFY (N=19,102) clinical trial history plus retinal HCN1 phosphenes and mid-2024 generic entry, propofol-site non-anesthetic HCN1 stabilizers and Florey/Petrou Org 34167 & allele-specific ASO programs, concrete narrow-window ABE9 (TRPM4 E7K c.19G>A guarding c.20A bystander; HCN1 G391D; HCN4 R524Q), CBE (S399P), and Prime Editing (HCN1 M305L/D401H transversions) blueprints, and HCN2/TBX18 biological pacemakers vs. dual-chamber/LBBAP pacing.

item.title: Fast-Spiking Fire, Big Potassium & The Scalloped Iris: KCNC1 MEAK, KCNA2, KCNMA1 & ITPR1 — Paradoxical Fever Rescue in KCNC1 R320H MEAK & One-Guide ABE Editing, 4-Aminopyridine GoF vs. LoF Polarity in KCNA2 Encephalopathy, Alcohol/Caffeine-Triggered KCNMA1 D434G/N999S PNKD3 Rescued by Lisdexamfetamine vs. Liang-Wang Syndrome, ITPR1 Dominant-Negative Gillespie Scalloped Aniridia vs. SCA15 Haploinsufficiency, 15/16 Tetramer-Poisoning Math & Autifony Therapeutics (AUT00201 / AUT00206) Biotech History (PDB 8F1C, 7PQT, 6V3G, 7LHE)
item.description: 5-Act One-Ångström-Tall Man Channelopathy, Base-Editor & Biotech History Treatise (Ep 2685) uniting four obligate homotetrameric cerebellar/myoclonus/BK channelopathies across four verified RCSB PDB cryo-EM structures: human Kv3.1 + positive allosteric modulator X9T/Compound 4 + K+ + Zn2+ + POV (PDB 8F1C, 2.92 Å, Chen et al., PNAS 2023, PMID 37812700), apo human Kv3.1 (PDB 7PQT, 2.65 Å, Botte et al., PNAS Nexus 2022, PMID 36741467), Ca2+-free human BK/Slo1 KCNMA1 (PDB 6V3G, 4.0 Å, Tao & MacKinnon, eLife 2019, PMID 31815672), and full-length tetrameric ER IP3R1 in lipid nanodisc with PLX & Zn2+ (PDB 7LHE, 3.3 Å, Baker et al., Commun Biol 2021). Covers four clinical cases & testing traps (MEAK KCNC1 p.Arg320His paradoxical fever improvement vs. seizure-free p.Arg339* NMD haploinsufficiency; KCNA2 LoF vs. GoF ClinVar polarity & Hedrich/Lerche 2021 4-AP rescue vs. Wu et al. 2026 SUDEP; KCNMA1 D434G/N999S alcohol/caffeine PNKD3 rescued by lisdexamfetamine vs. Liang-Wang LoF & Moldenhauer/Meredith 2024 KMS VUS score; ITPR1 Gillespie scalloped aniridia dominant-negative pore variants vs. SCA15 deletion haploinsufficiency & Romaniello 2022 83% superior cerebellar atrophy MRI clue), 35+ verified interatomic distances (Kv3.1 R4 ARG320–PHE256 2.84/3.10 Å, TLGYG filter, X9T–PRO373 2.14 Å & POV603 2.33 Å, T1 ZN601 2.30/1.93 Å; BK TVGYG, RCK1 ASP434–ASN465 2.42 Å, Ca2+ bowl ASP895; IP3R1 GGVGD GLY2547–ARG2544(D) 3.64 Å & ASP2551 3.94 Å, S6 gate LEU2582–PHE2586 3.06 Å, PLX 2.88 Å, C2H2 Zn2+ 1.71–2.32 Å), two spoken calculation pauses (15/16 binomial tetramer poisoning 6.25% vs. 50% haploinsufficiency vs. 40% ABE binary rescue 43.75%; PV+ fast-spiking interneuron repolarization t_repol 0.52 ms -> 2.08 ms & f_max 355 Hz -> 135 Hz -> 287 Hz PAM / 355 Hz ABE), single-guide ABE for KCNC1 c.959G>A and opposite-strand CBE for KCNMA1 c.1301A>G, KCIAF patient advocacy, and Autifony Therapeutics biotech history (2011 GSK spinout, QUIET-1 tinnitus futility, EUR 627.5M Boehringer deal & AUT00206 gamma/FDOPA biomarkers, 2020 returned rights, AUT00201 MEAK Ph1b NCT05873062 & USD 770.5M Jazz deal).

item.title: One Ångström Inside the Base Editor: ABE8e, CBE, DddA, Split-Intein Dual-AAV & the Five Unique DNA Base-Editing Strategies for Ion Channelopathies — One-Ångström atomic walks inside ABE8e (6VPC), TadA*8.20 (8E2P), human APOBEC3A E72A (5SWW), and mitochondrial DddA E1347A (8E5E); dual-AAV Poisson co-transduction & bystander vs. homotetramer w^4 calculation pauses; SCN8A R1872W, TMC1 Baringo, CFTR R553X/R1162X, KCNC1 R320H, CACNA1C BE-SKIP & RYR2/KCNT1 iSTOP; Beam (BEAM-101/BEAM-302), Verve/Eli Lilly USD 1.3B (VERVE-102) & Broad vs. CVC Cas9 IP royalty stacking
item.description: Wave 11 Flagship Episode CHAN_21 (Ep 2687): Complete five-act One-Ångström-Tall Man biophysical, clinical, and biotech-history treatise on DNA Base Editing for Ion Channelopathies. Explains why giant channel CDS (>4.7 kb AAV limit), dominant-negative tetramers, and post-mitotic DSB/HDR failure broke classical gene therapy and Cas9 nucleases; walks at 1 Å inside four verified experimental structures — PDB 6VPC (3.2 Å ABE8e + R-loop + 8AZ26 + Zn2+/Mg2+, explicitly noting SpCas9 D10A = Ala207 +197 offset, Glu59, Val106, Asn108, and 590–1,100-fold kinetic turbocharger T111R Arg111 at 2.33 Å), PDB 8E2P (2.72 Å TadA*8.20 + ssDNA UEL9 showing the 2.70 Å hairpin U-turn behind the 4–8 editing window and CBE-T evolution), PDB 5SWW (3.151 Å human APOBEC3A E72A trapped + ssDNA + Zn2+ + UGI biology), and PDB 8E5E (2.62 Å bacterial toxin DddA E1347A + dsDNA tandem base-displacement unlocking CRISPR-free mitochondrial DdCBE and TALED editing); dissects all Five Unique Channelopathy Base-Editing Strategies (Direct Reversion for SCN8A R1872W, TMC1 Baringo c.545A>G, KCNC1 R320H, CFTR R553X/R1162X/W1282X; PAM-flexible SpG/SpRY & narrow-window V106W/ABE9/YE1/CBE-T/OpenABE bystander shielding; BE-SKIP splice disruption for CACNA1C Timothy exon 8A; allele-specific iSTOP silencing for dominant GoF RYR2/KCNT1/CLCN7; and Split-Intein Dual-AAV vs. eVLP vs. GalNAc-LNP/PNP delivery); includes two spoken Calculation Pauses (Dual-AAV packaging budget & Poisson co-transduction at MOI = 2 vs. MOI = 5; bystander purity ABE8e vs. ABE9 & homotetramer w^4 vs. monomeric editing thresholds); traces David Liu lab -> Beam Therapeutics (2017 founding, 2020 IPO, Pfizer USD 1.35B deal, Lilly USD 600M Verve opt-in buyout, BEAM-101 BEACON pivotal Nov 2026 & BEAM-302 18-month AATD readouts) -> Verve Therapeutics (VERVE-101 Apr 2024 LNP pause -> VERVE-102 GalNAc-LNP NEJM 2026 -> Eli Lilly USD 1.3B 2025 acquisition) and the Broad vs. CVC Cas9 + Beam deaminase IP royalty stack; debunks base-editing myths and designs the decisive post-onset SCN8A structural and in vivo experiment.

item.title: The Synaptic Polarity Flip: SCN2A Age-Bifurcation, GABAA & GRIN (NMDA) Channelopathies — One-Ångström cryo-EM walks inside human NaV1.2 (6J8E), α1β3γ2L GABAA with GABA & diazepam (6HUP), and GluN1-GluN2B NMDA with S-ketamine (7EU8) vs. memantine (7SAD); Bayesian <3-mo SCN2A & Woodhull Mg2+ pauses; phenytoin, vigabatrin hypersensitivity, L-serine, memantine, elsunersen, radiprodil & adolescent CRISPRa
item.description: Wave 10 Channelopathies Episode 8 (Ep 2668 / CHAN_08): Five-act One-Ångström-Tall Man medical and biophysical treatise uniting the synaptic gain-of-function vs. loss-of-function polarity flip across SCN2A/NaV1.2 (<3-month neonatal GoF rescued by high-dose phenytoin vs. >3-month LoF ASD/late spasms worsened by sodium-channel blockers + p.Arg853Gln DII-S4 gating-pore/LoF paradox), GABAA (GABRB3 GoF vigabatrin hypersensitivity [Absalom et al. 2020/2022] vs. GABRA1/GABRB3/GABRG2 LoF trafficking/NMD escape [Macdonald/Kang; Johannesen; Maillard 2022; Zhou 2022; Liu 2023]), and GRIN/NMDA (GRIN1/GRIN2A/GRIN2B GoF polymicrogyria & DEE treated with memantine/radiprodil vs. GRIN LoF & epilepsy-aphasia rescued by oral L-serine 500 mg/kg/day). Walks at 1 Å through verified RCSB PDB structures 6J8E (3.0 Å NaV1.2-β2-KIIIA), 6HUP (3.58 Å α1β3γ2L GABAA-GABA-DZP-PIP2), 7EU8 (4.07 Å GluN1-GluN2B-S-ketamine), and 7SAD (3.96 Å GluN1a-GluN2B-memantine); includes two spoken calculation pauses (Bayesian <3-mo SCN2A polarity LR + mature pyramidal Kv-AHP hyperexcitability paradox; Woodhull NMDA Mg2+ block at -70 vs -20 mV & memantine vs. ATD-allosteric radiprodil); and integrates verified clinical trials (EMBRAVE NCT05737784/NCT07019922 elsunersen, EMBOLD NCT05818553 relutrigine, nL-SCN2A-002 NCT06314490, Honeycomb NCT05818943 & Beeline NCT07224581 radiprodil, NCT07941206, TAP-GRIN NCT07377032 L-serine) plus Tamura/Ahituv/Bender Nature 2025 adolescent SCN2A CRISPRa rescue.

item.title: The Burning-Pain Mirror: Inherited Erythromelalgia (IEM), Paroxysmal Extreme Pain Disorder (PEPD), TRPA1 FEPS & NaV1.8 Selective Analgesia (Suzetrigine) — One-Ångström cryo-EM walks inside human NaV1.7 (7W9K), NaV1.8 (7WFW/7WE4), and TRPA1 (6V9W/6PQO), Waxman's sympathetic-nociceptor NaV1.8 paradox, SCN11A L811P vs. L811F, carbamazepine in PEPD & S241T, suzetrigine (VX-548), BHV-7000, and AAV9 NaV1.7 epigenetic repression
item.description: Wave 10 Channelopathies Episode 10 (Ep 2670): Five-act One-Ångström-Tall Man medical and biophysical treatise on peripheral pain channelopathies (SCN9A Inherited Erythromelalgia IEM and Paroxysmal Extreme Pain Disorder PEPD, SCN10A/SCN11A small-fiber neuropathy and FEPS including the SCN11A p.Leu811Pro CIP vs. p.Leu811Phe FEPS codon-811 fork, and TRPA1 p.Asn855Ser FEPS1 including 2026 Schwann-cell 4-HNE signaling) plus NaV1.8 VSD2-selective non-opioid analgesia (suzetrigine / VX-548 / Journavx, approved 30 Jan 2025). Anchored to five verified RCSB PDB cryo-EM structures (7W9K with transparent +11 exon 11A offset in DII-DIV, 7WFW, 7WE4, 6V9W, 6PQO), two spoken calculation pauses (DRG Boltzmann -12 mV shift & sympathetic NaV1.8 depolarization-block paradox; suzetrigine free plasma target occupancy at NaV1.8 vs. cardiac NaV1.5), verified ClinicalTrials.gov studies (NAVIGATE 1/2 NCT05553366/NCT05558410, NCT05818852, NCT06628908, NCT02214615, NCT07262268, NCT05917912, NCT01769274, NCT02917187, NCT04039633), and emerging Kv7.2/7.3 bypass openers and AAV9 ZFP-KRAB NaV1.7 epigenetic silencing.

item.title: When the Folding Clock Breaks: Cystic Fibrosis (CFTR Classes I-VI), Trikafta & Alyftrek Rescue, and the Modulator-Ineligible 10% Frontier — One-Ångström cryo-EM walks inside human CFTR (5UAK apo, 6MSM ATP-dimerized, 8EIQ ΔF508 bound to tezacaftor CV6, elexacaftor WJX & ivacaftor VX7), sweat-duct vs. airway Cl-/HCO3- & NPD physics, ΔΔG folding math, SKYLINE/RIDGELINE Alyftrek, and Class I mRNA/AAV/ACE-tRNA/prime editing
item.description: Wave 10 Channelopathies Episode 11 (Ep 2671 / CHAN_11): Five-act One-Ångström-Tall Man medical and biophysical treatise on Cystic Fibrosis (CFTR / ABCC7 Classes I-VI), contrasting severe newborn F508del/F508del meconium ileus (sweat Cl- 104 mmol/L), adult R117H-5T CBAVD/recurrent pancreatitis (sweat Cl- 42 mmol/L), and modulator-ineligible Class I G542X/W1282X; tracing Dorothy Andersen (1938), Paul di Sant'Agnese (1953), Gibson & Cooke (1959), Paul Quinton (1983), Tsui/Riordan/Collins (1989), Beekman rectal organoid FIS (2013), and Jue Chen's human CFTR cryo-EM trilogy (PDB 5UAK, 6MSM, 8EIQ with CV6 tezacaftor, WJX elexacaftor, VX7 ivacaftor); featuring two spoken calculation pauses (sweat-duct vs. airway Cl-/HCO3- polarity, Henderson-Hasselbalch ASL pH 7.20->6.62 & NPD Wilschanski index; Boltzmann ddG folding synergy & multiplicative N_surf x P_o rescue math), verified Phase 3 evidence (Ramsey 2011, Wainwright 2015, Middleton 2019, Heijerman 2019, Mall 2022, Burgel 2024, SKYLINE 102/103 & RIDGELINE 2025), One Medicine CF pig/ferret proofs, and verified Class I 10% frontier trials (NCT05668741 VX-522, NCT06237335 RCT2100, NCT05248230 4D-710, NCT06526923 SP-101, NCT06515002/NCT06962852 BI 3720931, Ahern ACE-tRNAs, Bulcaen 2024 prime editing).

item.title: Salt, Sugar, and One Broken Atom: Renal Tubular (Bartter, Gitelman, EAST/SeSAME, PHA1) & Endocrine K_ATP Neonatal Diabetes / DEND Channelopathies — Genetic lifelong furosemide vs. thiazide (+8 mV TAL paracellular Ca2+ physics, urine Cl-/Ca2+/Cr triage & MLPA), EAST/SeSAME Kir4.1 vs. Kir5.1, PHA1 vs. Liddle ENaC mirrors, One-Ångström cryo-EM walks inside human NCC (8FHT, 8VPN + indapamide/WNK-SPAK) and pancreatic K_ATP (6BAA + glibenclamide, 6C3O + MgADP), and high-dose oral sulfonylurea transfer freeing 93% of KCNJ11 children from insulin needles
item.description: Wave 10 Channelopathies Episode 12 (Ep 2672): Five-act One-Ångström-Tall Man medical and biophysical treatise uniting Renal Tubular Channelopathies (Antenatal/Classic Bartter Types I–V [SLC12A1/NKCC2, KCNJ1/ROMK transient neonatal hyperkalemia, CLCNKB, BSND/Barttin deafness, MAGED2], Gitelman Syndrome [SLC12A3/NCC, 6% Alu MLPA rearrangements, Gordon/FHHt WNK-SPAK mirror], EAST/SeSAME [KCNJ10/Kir4.1 vs. KCNJ16/Kir5.1 acidosis], and Systemic PHA1B [SCNN1A/B/G ENaC LoF mirror of Liddle Syndrome]) with the Endocrine K_ATP Mirror (KCNJ11/ABCC8 GoF Permanent Neonatal Diabetes & iDEND/DEND Syndrome vs. Congenital Hyperinsulinism). Grounded in four verified RCSB PDB cryo-EM structures (8FHT [3.02 Å human NCC + Na+/Cl-], 8VPN [2.7 Å phosphorylated human NCC + indapamide BL1 + WNK-SPAK TPO55/TPO60/SEP73 + CTD ATP, -1 isoform numbering offset], 6BAA [3.63 Å Kir6.2/SUR1 K_ATP + ATP + glibenclamide GBM at ARG1246 2.80 Å], and 6C3O [3.9 Å human K_ATP quatrefoil + K+ TIGFG + SUR1 MgADP 1.89 Å / MgATP 1.98 Å]), two spoken calculation pauses (+8 mV lumen-positive TAL paracellular divalent Boltzmann factor & uCa/uCr + uCl- differential; p.Arg201His 30x IC50(ATP) shift locking beta-cell V_m at -80.7 mV and 0.5-1.5 mg/kg/day glibenclamide transfer physics with zero severe hypoglycemia), all 15 dossier PMIDs / 10 PMCIDs, and all 14 verified ClinicalTrials.gov NCT trials (NCT02624817 10-year 93% durable insulin independence, NCT00334711, NCT02624830, NCT05751525, NCT02921906, NCT00321321, NCT06065852, NCT03847571, NCT04995627, NCT01146197, NCT00822107, NCT00276289, NCT02297048, NCT02035046).

item.title: When the Heart Forgets How to Reset: Congenital Long QT Syndrome (LQT1, LQT2, LQT3 & Jervell-Lange-Nielsen) — One-Ångström cryo-EM walks inside human KCNQ1-KCNE1-PIP2 (9VEC/9VEI), hERG (5VA1/7CN1), and NaV1.5 (6UZ3/7DTC), Bazett vs. Fridericia & late-I_NaL physics, nadolol, mexiletine in LQT2, lumacaftor-ivacaftor, and SupRep AAV9 gene therapy

item.title: Shoulders of Giants — Neuropharmacology & Bioenergetics: Nicotinic Allostery, SARM1/NAMPT & Rescuing Axons After Blast TBI & Metabolic Stress
item.description: Five-Act historical and biophysical exploration of two intertwined neuropharmacological frontiers: (1) selective alpha-7 and alpha-4-beta-2 nicotinic acetylcholine receptor allostery and desensitization in prefrontal cognitive dysfunction (from Loewi, Changeux & Freedman to Cincotta, Yorek MS et al. 2008 and modern PAM/muscarinic therapeutics), and (2) the Wallerian degeneration WldS/SARM1/NAMPT NAD+ survival switch—showing how subclinical pattern-ERG diagnostics after blast-mediated traumatic brain injury identify a therapeutic window where the NAMPT activator P7C3-S243 prevents chronic visual loss (Dutca, Pieper, Harper et al. 2014, PMC5102342) alongside NRK1/2 nicotinamide riboside salvage (Trammell, Brenner et al. 2016, PMC4882590).

item.title: Shoulders of Giants — Nociceptor Ion Channels: Complement C5a/C3a, TRPV1, TRPM8 & Tetrodotoxin-Resistant Na+ Channels in Pain
item.description: Five-Act biophysical journey from Bordet & Ehrlich's discovery of complement (1899), David Julius's cloning of TRPV1 (1997), Ardem Patapoutian's TRPM8 (2002), and Waxman/Wood's TTX-resistant nociceptor sodium channels (NaV1.8/NaV1.9) to collaborative studies revealing how C5a and C3a anaphylatoxins sensitize cutaneous heat and mechanical nociceptors via TRPV1 and NGF (Jang, Usachev, Brennan et al. 2010, Pain, PMC2814960), how natriuretic peptides vs IL-6 cytokines modulate cardiac nociceptive TRPV1 and TTXr-Na+ currents (Mohapatra, Usachev, Yorek MS 2011), and how corneal C-fiber TRPM8 osmosensing measures small-fiber integrity (PMC5113984).

item.title: Shoulders of Giants — Host Defense & Immunity: Leishmania CXCL1 Proteolysis, Neutrophil CD47/SHP-1 Brakes & CD4 Enhancer Demethylation
item.description: Five-Act immunological detective story tracing three fundamental checkpoints of innate and adaptive immunity: (1) from Mosmann & Coffman's 1986 Th1/Th2 Leishmania major paradigm to selective parasite metalloprotease cleavage of murine CXCL1 (PMC6625741) and the temporal IL-4 instruction paradox (PMC7640617); (2) from motheaten Ptpn6/SHP-1 mutant mice and Weissman's CD47 checkpoint to proving CD47 halts Ptpn6-deficient neutrophils from provoking lethal RIPK1/IL-1 autoinflammation (Science Advances 2023, PMC9821860); and (3) from Littman's Cd4 silencer/enhancer architecture and Rao's TET dioxygenases to stimulus-responsive DNA demethylation sustaining effector CD4 T-cell identity (Nature Communications 2022, PMC8933563).

item.title: Shoulders of Giants — Ion Channels & Gene Editing: NaV1.6 (SCN8A), Parvalbumin Interneuron Failure & Adenine Base Editing Rescue of Epilepsy
item.description: Five-Act biophysical and genetic capstone tracing voltage-gated sodium channels from Hodgkin & Huxley (1952), Catterall's DIII-DIV IFM fast-inactivation latch, Raman & Bean's resurgent Na+ current (1997), Miriam Meisler's cloning of Scn8a (NaV1.6) and discovery of human SCN8A developmental and epileptic encephalopathy (2012), and Gaudelli & David Liu's invention of CRISPR Adenine Base Editors (2017) to recent brain-slice electrophysiology proving how gain-of-function SCN8A drives parvalbumin interneurons into premature depolarization block and synaptic failure (Miralles, Patel et al. 2024 JCI Insight, PMC11529981) and in vivo AAV adenine base editing rewriting R1872W back to wild-type to rescue seizures and sudden unexpected death in epilepsy (Reever, Meisler, Farber, Patel et al. 2026 JCI, PMC12871382).

item.title: Shoulders of Giants — Mark A. Yorek (IV): Superoxide, Peroxynitrite & the Vasopeptidase Shield — NEP, CGRP & Neurovascular Rescue (2000–2018)
item.description: Episode IV of the 6-part On the Shoulders of Giants series honoring Dr. Mark Anthony Yorek: dissecting the diffusion-limited collision of superoxide (O2.-) with nitric oxide (k ~ 1.9 x 10^10 M^-1 s^-1) to form peroxynitrite (ONOO-) inside epineurial arterioles (Coppey et al. 2001, Diabetes, 469 citations; Obrosova, Pacher, Szabo & Yorek collaborations on PARP-1 & FeTMPyP/MnTBAP, PMC5321249), and Yorek's pioneering discovery that upregulated neutral endopeptidase (NEP / neprilysin) degrades vasodilatory CGRP and natriuretic peptides—rescued by dual ACE/NEP vasopeptidase inhibition (AVE7688 / ilepatril, Diabetes, Hypertension, PMC2817866, PMC2933895) and genetic NEP-/- knockout mice (PMC7714044, co-authored with Matthew S. Yorek).

item.title: Shoulders of Giants — Mark A. Yorek (VI): Forty Years Back to Omega-3 — Resolvin D1, Nerve Regeneration & Horizons to 2050
item.description: Episode VI (Grand Finale) of the 6-part On the Shoulders of Giants series honoring Dr. Mark Anthony Yorek's 45-year career (1980–2026): how the 1983–1985 DHA neural lipid discoveries with Art Spector came full circle 30–40 years later when Mark Yorek, Lawrence Coppey, Eric Davidson, Alexander Obrosov, and Matthew S. Yorek proved that omega-3 menhaden oil, 15-lipoxygenase-1 metabolites (Resolvin D1 / E1, neuroprotectin D1), and salsalate acetylation synergy don't merely slow diabetic neuropathy—they actively regenerate vanished corneal and intraepidermal nerve fibers, protect disuse skeletal muscle atrophy (2025, PMC12747565), establish rational combination therapy (2024–2025, PMC11133577, PMC12292556, PMC12341837), and inspire the 2026–2050 precision neurovascular regeneration era.

Drug development, human trials and bedside interpretation draw on separate sources. Pharmacology notebook · Primary capillary experiment

item.title: The Fracture the Scan Didn't Predict — Alendronate Hydroxyapatite Binding & Osteoclast FPPS Inhibition (PDB 2F92), FIT Hip Fracture Reduction, CTX/P1NP Turnover Markers & Atypical Subtrochanteric Femoral Fracture
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 117: Alendronate Hydroxyapatite Binding & Osteoclast FPPS Inhibition (PDB 2F92), FIT Hip Fracture Reduction, CTX/P1NP Turnover Markers & Atypical Subtrochanteric Femoral Fracture. A woman’s hip density improved during alendronate treatment. Seven years after she started, a new ache down the outside of her thigh brings her back. The starting chapter, *Bone and Joints* in the 2013 third edition of *Haschek and Rousseaux’s Handbook of Toxicologic Pathology*, includes alendronate in an ovariectomized rat model and discusses bone remodeling, markers and atypical fractures. Use the animal material for mechanism and the linked human sources for clinical outcomes. Pharmacology notebook

item.title: The Drug That Had to Reach the Colon — Azad Khan's 1977 Sulfasalazine Split Experiment, pH-Dependent Eudragit & MMX Mesalamine Colonic Delivery, Fecal Calprotectin vs. Mucosal Endoscopy & Interstitial Nephritis Surveillance
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 120: Azad Khan's 1977 Sulfasalazine Split Experiment, pH-Dependent Eudragit & MMX Mesalamine Colonic Delivery, Fecal Calprotectin vs. Mucosal Endoscopy & Interstitial Nephritis Surveillance. An oral drug can reach the bloodstream and still deliver little to the tissue it is meant to treat. Mesalamine turns that problem into a historical experiment. First separate the two products of sulfasalazine, then find a way to bring the active one back to inflamed colonic mucosa. The starting source is Chapter Four, *Mucosal Healing in Ulcerative Colitis: Pathophysiology and Pharmacology*, in *Advances in Clinical Chemistry* (2013). Its discussion of 5-aminosalicylic acid and epithelial restitution leads into the original experiments. Pharmacology notebook

item.description: From nociceptor channel cloning to reversible peripheral nerve-ending remodeling: Caterina et al.'s (1997) expression cloning of the heat- and capsaicin-gated cation channel TRPV1, Kennedy et al.'s (2010) serial skin-punch biopsies quantifying ~80% reversible PGP 9.5 epidermal nerve-fiber loss and 24-week regeneration after a 60-minute 8% capsaicin patch, and contrasting Backonja (2008, low-dose active control in PHN) vs. Bischoff (2014, inert placebo in post-herniorrhaphy pain) RCT outcomes.

item.title: The Heart Block and the Falling Glucose — Verapamil Overdose AV Dissociation & Metabolic Shock, High-Dose Insulin Euglycemic Therapy (Kline 1993; Yuan 1999) & Poison-Center Evidence
item.description: Cardiovascular-metabolic coupling in severe L-type calcium-channel blocker poisoning: Malakian et al.'s (2026) verapamil dysrhythmia and hypoinsulinemic hyperglycemia trajectory, Kline et al.'s (1993) controlled canine survival comparison of insulin-dextrose vs. calcium, epinephrine, and glucagon, Yuan et al.'s (1999) early human high-dose insulin euglycemic case series, and Cole et al.'s (2018) 199-patient poison-center chart review of hypoglycemia and hypokalemia risks.

item.title: The Drug That Quieted the First Wave — Ondansetron & Cisplatin Emesis, 5-HT3A Cryo-EM (PDB 6W1M), Acute 5-HT3 vs. Delayed Substance P/NK1 Phase, hERG QTc Risk & CYP2D6 CPIC
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology of ondansetron and biphasic chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting: Cubeddu & Marty's 1990 cisplatin trials, 2.8 Å cryo-EM structure of 5-HT3A bound to ondansetron (PDB 6W1M), why acute (0–24h) peripheral 5-HT3 vagal signaling gives way to delayed (24–120h) central NK1/Substance P signaling, hERG K+ channel blockade and FDA IV dose caps, and CPIC CYP2D6 ultrarapid metabolizer guidance.

item.title: The Venom That Took the Spinal Route — Intrathecal Ziconotide (ω-Conotoxin MVIIA), Olivera's Conus magus Discovery, Human CaV2.2 Cryo-EM Pore Plug (PDB 7MIX) & Slow Titration
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology of intrathecal ziconotide (PRIALT / omega-conotoxin MVIIA): Olivera's discovery of Conus magus peptide toxins, Nieng Yan's 3.1 Å cryo-EM structure of human CaV2.2 plugged by ziconotide (PDB 7MIX), why systemic IV delivery causes orthostatic hypotension via sympathetic CaV2.2 block while intrathecal delivery targets dorsal horn lamina I/II synapses without tolerance or respiratory depression, and Staats (2004) vs. Rauck (2006) titration kinetics.

item.title: The Amino Acid at the Brain's Gate — Six-Competitor Plasma Tryptophan Ratio, Human LAT1 Cryo-EM (8J8M/8XPU), TPH2 & PET Tracer Assumptions, Delgado's Remission Relapse Trials (14/21; 8/15 vs. 1/15) & Breakfast Limits
item.description: From plasma amino-acid competition at blood-brain barrier LAT1–CD98hc (PDB 8J8M L-Trp & 8XPU JPH203) to acute tryptophan depletion trials: UHPLC-MS/MS separation of isobaric Leu/Ile, recombinant TPH2 kinetics vs. alpha-[11C]methyl-L-Trp PET assumptions, Delgado's remitted depression crossover (14/21) and SSRI vs. desipramine responder split (8/15 vs. 1/15), and why Wurtman's breakfast study measured plasma ratios rather than mood.

item.title: The Gluten Fragment That Changed Its Charge — Celiac TG2 Cys277 Gln→Glu Deamidation, HLA-DQ2.5 Lysβ71 Pocket (1S9V), Irreversible ZED1227 Active-Site Trapping & Gluten-Challenge Biopsy Trials
item.description: Atomic pathogenesis and covalent enzyme inhibition in celiac disease: tissue transglutaminase 2 (TG2) Cys277 thioester deamidation of gliadin glutamine into negatively charged glutamate, HLA-DQ2.5 positively charged P4/P6/P7 pocket anchoring via Lysβ71 (PDB 1S9V), tTG-IgA vs. total IgA and Marsh/villus-height-to-crypt-depth morphometry, and Schuppan et al.'s (2021) NEJM ZED1227 trial.

item.title: The Bowel That Learned to Absorb Again — Short-Bowel High-Output Jejunostomy Secretory Losses, GLP-2R Cryo-EM & Teduglutide Ala2→Gly2 DPP-4 Shielding & STEPS Parenteral Weaning
item.description: Intestinal rehabilitation in short-bowel syndrome with end-jejunostomy: net secretory stoma sodium/water balance vs. renal sodium conservation, colonic salvage anatomy, human GLP-2–GLP-2R–Gs cryo-EM structure and teduglutide Ala2→Gly2 DPP-4 resistance, villus height/crypt depth trophic remodeling, and Jeppesen's STEPS randomized parenteral-support reduction trial.

item.title: The Calabar Bean & the Missing Signal — Physostigmine, Acetylcholinesterase Ser203 Carbamylation, Antimuscarinic Delirium & QRS Counterfactuals
item.description: From Efik esere ordeal records in Old Calabar and Thomas Richard Fraser's Edinburgh experiments to human acetylcholinesterase Ser203 carbamylation (4EY4/1GQR), false-positive urine TCA immunoassays, and ECG QRS gating in antimuscarinic delirium.

item.title: How a Blood Vessel Tells Itself to Relax — Furchgott & Zawadzki's 1980 Intact vs. Rubbed Rabbit Aorta, Rubanyi's Donor-Detector Perfusion, Palmer & Moncada's Ozone Chemiluminescence Nitric Oxide Proof & 15N-Arginine Tracing
item.description: How the vascular endothelium's relaxing signal was identified as nitric oxide: Furchgott & Zawadzki's (1980) discovery that removing the inner endothelial lining abolishes acetylcholine relaxation while preserving smooth-muscle contraction, Rubanyi et al.'s (1985) upstream donor/downstream denuded detector bioassay, Palmer, Ferrige & Moncada's (1987) chemiluminescent nitric oxide measurement alongside Ignarro's cGMP comparison, and 15N-arginine precursor tracing.

item.title: How Cells Tie Growth to Available Nutrients — Heitman & Hall's Yeast FPR1/TOR1/TOR2 Rapamycin Mutants, Sabatini & Brown's Mammalian mTOR Affinity Capture & Hara's Amino-Acid Withdrawal Gate
item.description: Discovery of the TOR nutrient-sensing pathway: Heitman, Movva & Hall (1991) genetic screen in Saccharomyces cerevisiae showing rapamycin requires FKBP12 (FPR1) to inhibit TOR1/TOR2, Sabatini et al. (1994) & Brown et al. (1994) biochemical capture of the ~289 kDa mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR) only when rapamycin is bound to FKBP12, Barbet et al. (1996) starvation-like translation arrest, and Hara et al. (1998) amino-acid gating of insulin-stimulated p70S6K phosphorylation.

item.title: How a Cell Passes a Message Inside — Sutherland & Rall's Broken-Cell Liver Homogenate Fractionation, Heat-Stable Cyclic AMP Transfer & Walsh's cAMP-Dependent Protein Kinase
item.description: Discovery of the second-messenger principle: Rall, Sutherland & Berthet (1957) two-stage cell-free assay separating particulate membrane hormone response from soluble phosphorylase activation via a dialyzable, heat-stable factor, Sutherland & Rall (1958) chemical identification of cyclic 3',5'-AMP, and Walsh, Perkins & Krebs (1968) discovery of cAMP-dependent protein kinase (PKA).

item.title: The Mirror-Image Test for an Opioid Receptor — Goldstein's Stereospecificity, Pert & Snyder's [3H]Naloxone Levorphanol vs. Dextrorphan Assay & Enkephalin Discovery
item.description: Biochemical proof of brain opioid receptors: Goldstein et al. (1971) enantiomeric competition concept, Pert & Snyder (1973) [3H]naloxone vacuum-filtration assay showing stereospecific displacement by (-)-levorphanol but not (+)-dextrorphan, Hughes et al. (1975) discovery of endogenous pentapeptides Met- and Leu-enkephalin, and 1992 delta-receptor cloning.

item.itunes:title: The Discovery of the Opiate Receptor — Candace Pert & Receptor Biophysics

item.itunes:title: The Accidental Discovery of Second Messengers — Tap Water Ca2+, GTP Clocks & Nitric Oxide

item.title: The Signal the Poison Interrupted — Delayed Belladonna Atropine Rebound via LC-MS/MS, Scopolamine Hippocampal Theta Disruption & Physostigmine vs. Lorazepam in Antimuscarinic Delirium
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology investigation of central and peripheral muscarinic blockade: delayed gastrointestinal absorption and day-4 LC-MS/MS serum atropine rebound after belladonna ingestion (Hayashi et al. 2026), human intracranial EEG evidence of scopolamine disrupting hippocampal theta oscillations during memory encoding (Gedankien et al. 2023), and randomized trial evidence comparing physostigmine cholinesterase inhibition against lorazepam sedation in antimuscarinic delirium.

item.title: The Pump at the Brain — Blood-Brain Barrier P-Glycoprotein (ABCB1) Efflux, Loperamide vs. Fentanyl CNS Exclusion, Cryo-EM ATPase Cycle & Drug-Drug Interactions
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology deep dive into blood-brain barrier ABCB1 (P-glycoprotein) efflux: why potent mu-opioid agonists like loperamide act peripherally unless P-gp is overwhelmed or inhibited, inward-to-outward cryo-EM peristaltic extrusion, and clinical transporter inhibition.

item.title: The Muscle That Waited — Prolonged Post-Succinylcholine Neuromuscular Blockade, Zero Train-of-Four Twitches, Dibucaine Number 41 vs. Catalytic BChE Activity & BCHE Genotyping
item.description: Pharmacogenetics and clinical management of prolonged succinylcholine apnea (Hubbell et al. 2025): why a short-acting depolarizing neuromuscular blocker lasted 8 hours after hip surgery, peripheral nerve stimulator absence of twitches, distinguishing quantitative butyrylcholinesterase deficiency from qualitative atypical variants via the dibucaine inhibition number, and BCHE sequencing.

item.title: The Letter the First Test Missed — Compound Heterozygous DPYD Variants Missed by 4-SNP Panels (de Haar-Holleman 2024), Fluorouracil Catabolism Collapse & Uridine Triacetate Antidote Rescue
item.description: Pharmacogenomics and biochemical rescue of fluoropyrimidine toxicity: why targeted 4-variant DPYD genotyping misses rare in-trans compound heterozygotes (de Haar-Holleman et al. 2024), phenotypic DPD uracil breath/plasma assays (Coenen et al. 2019), 5-FU catabolic shunting into FUTP/FdUMP (Peters et al. 1988), and emergency antidote rescue with uridine triacetate (Jacob et al. 2022).

item.title: The Drug That Cut the Drug — Glucarpidase Methotrexate Rescue, DAMPA Immunoassay Cross-Reactivity vs. HPLC/LC-MS/MS (5.79 vs. 2.27 µmol/L at Hour 117, Gulley 2020), Ogawa Tissue Rebound & Organ Recovery
item.description: Enzymatic drug cleavage and analytical cross-reactivity after high-dose methotrexate rescue with glucarpidase (carboxypeptidase G2): Gulley et al.'s (2020) split specimen 74 hours post-glucarpidase reading 5.79 µmol/L by immunoassay vs. 2.27 µmol/L by HPLC due to DAMPA metabolite persistence beyond the nominal 48-hour VORAXAZE label window, Ogawa et al.'s (2024) 98.83% 20-minute plasma drop and tissue rebound, and Corbisier et al.'s (2024) multimodal pediatric liver/renal recovery.

item.title: The Blood That Would Not Turn Red — Acquired Methemoglobinemia (SpO2 86% vs. PaO2 85 mmHg), Multi-Wavelength Co-Oximetry, NADPH Reductase & G6PD Methylene Blue Hemolysis
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology deep dive into acquired methemoglobinemia and antidote mechanics: why dual-wavelength pulse oximetry locks near 85–86% despite high dissolved arterial PaO2, multi-wavelength co-oximetry separation of ferric (Fe3+) methemoglobin, how methylene blue uses NADPH methemoglobin reductase as an artificial electron shuttle, and why G6PD deficiency converts methylene blue into a trigger for acute Heinz-body hemolysis (Mathiyalagan et al. 2025; ProvayBlue US label).

item.title: The Number the Antidote Raised — Digoxin Immune Fab Redistribution vs. Immunoassay Interference, Ultrafiltration Free Digoxin (Jortani 1999), Renal Rebound Kinetics (Ujhelyi 1993) & Chronic Cardiogenic Shock
item.description: Separating true pharmacokinetic tissue redistribution from platform-dependent immunoassay interference after digoxin immune Fab: Smith et al. (1976) 12-fold total serum rise with undetectable free digoxin, Jortani et al. (1999) ultrafiltrate immunoassay bias across platforms, Ujhelyi et al. (1993) delayed free-digoxin rebound in renal dysfunction, and Gerritsma et al. (2025) chronic digoxin cardiogenic shock.

item.title: The Antibiotic at the Other Ribosome — Linezolid Hyperlactatemia, Mitoribosome COX-II vs. Nuclear Tom20/SDHA Translation, Paired PBMC Recovery & Duration Cohort Denominators
item.description: Translational pharmacology and mitochondrial toxicology of oxazolidinone antibiotics: linezolid-associated hyperlactatemia despite 98% arterial oxygen saturation (Chaudhri et al. 2024, 4.9->5.1->1.6 mmol/L), selective depletion of mitoribosome-encoded cytochrome c oxidase subunits vs. nuclear-encoded Tom20 and SDHA in human HL-60/THP-1 cells (Milosevic et al. 2018), paired patient PBMC recovery (Garrabou et al. 2007, COX-II protein 16% and enzyme activity 51% of controls with intact mtDNA/mRNA), and 40-patient cross-sectional duration cohorts (Martínez-Guitián et al. 2026).

item.title: The Drug That Changed With the Fever — Clozapine 1975 Finland Cluster & Kane 1988 Trial, Human H4–Gi Structure (PDB 8JXV), CYP1A2 Inflammation/Smoking Shift & AGP Binding
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 82: from the 1975 Finnish agranulocytosis cluster (Idänpään-Heikkilä et al.) and Kane et al.'s (1988) treatment-resistant schizophrenia trial (38/126 vs. 5/141) to ancillary human H4-Gi cryo-EM structure (PDB 8JXV), why acute pneumonia and abrupt smoking cessation elevate serum clozapine and the clozapine:norclozapine ratio via IL-6 CYP1A2 suppression and de-induction (Faber & Fuhr; Dickmann; Raaska), alpha-1-acid glycoprotein (AGP) unbound-fraction buffering, and the June 2025 FDA clozapine REMS removal.

item.title: The Channel That Quieted Insulin — Congenital Hyperinsulinism Critical Samples, Diazoxide KATP Opening, SUR1/Kir6.2 Comparator (PDB 7W4O), KCNJ11 Genetics & Pulmonary Hypertension
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 81: neonatal hypoketotic hypoglycemia critical-sample diagnostics (simultaneous glucose, insulin, C-peptide, beta-hydroxybutyrate, and free fatty acids; Ferrara et al.), repurposing antihypertensive benzothiadiazine diazoxide (Drash & Wolff 1964), beta-cell SUR1/Kir6.2 KATP opening and NN414 comparator structure (PDB 7W4O), dominant KCNJ11 p.Phe55Leu gating vs. recessive focal 11p15 loss, and echocardiographic surveillance for diazoxide-associated pulmonary hypertension (Herrera et al., 7/295).

item.title: The Drug That Emptied the Vesicle — Rauwolfia & Reserpine Discovery, Human VMAT2 Cytoplasm-Facing Complex (PDB 8JTC), Orthostatic ΔHR/ΔSBP & Prolonged Monoamine Depletion
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 80: from Vakil's (1949) Rauwolfia root reports and Müller, Schlittler & Bein's (1952) reserpine isolation to V-ATPase 2H+:1 amine stoichiometry (Knoth et al.), human VMAT2-reserpine cytoplasm-facing cryo-EM coordinates (Wu et al. PDB 8JTC, Tyr341/Tyr433; Pidathala et al. PDB 8T6A), why noncovalent transporter blockade produces prolonged vesicular monoamine depletion and blunted orthostatic heart-rate compensation, and bounded interpretation of Freis's (1954) depression case series.

item.title: The Walk That Became a Seizure — Dalfampridine (4-AP) in Demyelinated Axons, Kv1.2/Kv2.1 Architecture (PDB 2R9R), Timed-Walk Trial Denominators & Renal Seizure Risk
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 77: dalfampridine (4-aminopyridine) conduction rescue in diphtheria-toxin demyelinated rat spinal roots (Bostock, Sherratt & Sears 1978–1981), Kv1.2/Kv2.1 paddle-chimera selectivity filter coordinates (PDB 2R9R, Val371/Gly372), Goodman et al. (2009, 2010) Phase 3 timed 25-foot walk responder denominators (78/224 vs. 6/72; 51/119 vs. 11/118), extended-release vs. oral solution Cmax, and why renal impairment (CrCl <= 50 mL/min) precipitates acute seizures.

item.title: The Rhythm the Drug Could Break — Dofetilide (Tikosyn) Inpatient QT Gate, Human hERG Cryo-EM Cavity (PDB 5VA2), Reverse Use-Dependence, Renal OCT2/MATE1 & the DIAMOND Trials
item.description: Biophysics, structural biology, and clinical safety engineering of dofetilide (Tikosyn): Sanguinetti's IKr/hERG discovery, Wang & MacKinnon's human Kv11.1 cryo-EM structure (PDB 5VA2) and Tyr652/Phe656 drug-trapping cavity, reverse use-dependence at slow sinus rates after cardioversion, renal OCT2/MATE1 transport interactions, and the DIAMOND trials.

item.title: The Cocaine Signal That Stayed Behind — Cocaine-Associated Chest Pain, Serial hs-cTnI Trajectory, Human DAT-Cocaine Cryo-EM (PDB 9EO4), Benzoylecgonine/Cocaethylene LC-MS/MS & Lange Vasospasm
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology & Forensic Toxicology of cocaine: why urine immunoassays detect hydrolytic metabolite benzoylecgonine for days after parent cocaine (T1/2 ~1h) has cleared, Nielsen et al.'s (2024) 2.66 Å cryo-EM structure of human DAT bound to cocaine (PDB 9EO4), hepatic carboxylesterase transesterification with ethanol to form long-acting cocaethylene, serial hs-cTnI rule-in, and Lange et al.'s (1989, 1990) coronary catheterization proof of alpha-adrenergic vasospasm.

item.title: The Spasticity Drug the Kidney Kept — Oral Baclofen Coma in CKD, Bowery's GABAB Discovery, Human GABAB1-GABAB2 Cryo-EM (PDB 4MS4/7EB2), Triphasic EEG & EXTRIP Hemodialysis
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology of baclofen neurotoxicity in renal impairment: Keberle's 1962 lipophilic GABA design and Bowery's 1980 GABAB receptor discovery, human GABAB1-GABAB2 heterodimer crystal/cryo-EM structures (PDB 4MS4, 7EB2), why 69–85% unchanged renal clearance causes rapid accumulation, triphasic/burst-suppression encephalopathy, and coma in CKD (Muanda et al. 2019), and EXTRIP guideline criteria for emergent hemodialysis.

item.title: The First Breath Caffeine Bought — Apnea of Prematurity, Aranda's 1977 Trial, Human A2A Receptor Cryo-EM/X-Ray (PDB 5MZP/5G53), CYP1A2 Ontogeny & CAP Trial Outcomes
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology of caffeine citrate in apnea of prematurity: central vs. obstructive vs. mixed apnea traces, Aranda et al. (1977) and Murat et al. (1981) clinical trials, human A2A receptor crystal structures (PDB 5MZP, 5G53) showing competitive adenosine blockade, neonatal CYP1A2 ontogeny (~100-hour T1/2 vs. 4–6 hours in adults) and 2:1 salt-to-base dosing safety, and the 2,006-infant CAP trial through age 11 (Schmidt et al. 2006, 2007, 2017).

item.title: The Drug That Changed the Ward — Chlorpromazine from Rhône-Poulenc Patent & 1952 Psychiatric Wards (Laborit, Delay & Elkes) to Pause-Triggered Torsades, Human hERG Cryo-EM (5VA1), DRD2 Kinetics & Sulfoxide LC-MS/MS
item.description: Two ward records seventy years apart: chlorpromazine's transition from Rhône-Poulenc synthesis (US2645640A) and Laborit's 1952 surgical 'artificial hibernation' to Delay & Deniker's psychiatric cases, Elkes & Elkes's 1954 crossover, and the 1964 NIMH Collaborative Study, paired with a contemporary pause-triggered torsades workup (Fridericia QTc 531 ms), ligand-free human hERG cryo-EM (PDB 5VA1), oocyte vs. CHO IC50s (21.6 vs. 1.47 µM), and DRD2 residence kinetics.

item.title: The Fat Droplet That Wouldn't Let Go — PNPLA3 I148M Droplet Sequestration & ABHD5 Competition, Romeo's Dallas Heart Study Scan, MRI-PDFF vs. FIB-4 & AZD2693 Antisense FORTUNA Trial
item.description: Why knocking out Pnpla3 in mice did not cause fatty liver while human PNPLA3 I148M drives steatohepatitis: Romeo et al. (2008) 1H-MRS genetics, Ser47–Asp166 patatin dyad, ubiquitylation-resistant I148M accumulation on lipid droplets sequestering CGI-58/ABHD5 away from ATGL (Wang et al. 2019), and phase I/IIb GalNAc-ASO AZD2693 MRI-PDFF reductions vs. FORTUNA histologic fibrosis endpoints.

item.title: The First Calories Back — Refeeding Syndrome, Insulin-Driven Phosphate/Potassium Shifts, PDH E1 ThDP Geometry (1NI4) & Doig ICU Trial
item.description: From starvation to refeeding syndrome in the ICU: insulin-stimulated Na+/K+-ATPase potassium uptake and intracellular phosphate trapping, human pyruvate dehydrogenase E1 thiamine diphosphate (ThDP) active-site geometry (PDB 1NI4), whole-blood ThDP LC-MS/MS assays, diaphragmatic weakness in hypophosphatemia (Aubier 1985), and the Doig et al. (2015) caloric restriction trial.

item.title: Warfarin & the Three Clocks of Bleeding — Spoiled Sweet Clover, VKORC1 Asn80/Tyr139, Chiral S/R-Warfarin m/z 307→161, 4F-PCC vs. INR & Serial ICH CT
item.description: From spoiled sweet-clover hemorrhagic disease and Link's 1947 patent to human VKORC1 Asn80/Tyr139 crystal contacts, chiral LC-MS/MS separation of S- and R-warfarin (sharing m/z 307->161), and separating the three clinical clocks of drug clearance, factor replacement (4F-PCC vs. plasma), and intracerebral hematoma expansion.

item.title: The Blue Dye & the Oxygen Number — Methylene Blue, Acquired Methemoglobinemia, Two-Wavelength SpO2 vs. Co-Oximetry & G6PD Limits
item.description: How an industrial phenothiazine dye became the antidote for acquired methemoglobinemia—and why both ferric methemoglobin (660/940 nm) and intravenous methylene blue itself spoof two-wavelength pulse oximeters toward an ~85% plateau while multiwavelength co-oximetry separates fractional species.

item.title: Why a Pulse Oximeter Needs a Pulse — Millikan & Wood's Bloodless Ear Zero, Takuo Aoyagi's 1974 Pulsatile AC/DC Ratio, Dyshemoglobin 85% Artifacts & Skin-Pigment Bias
item.description: Optical physics and physiological limitations of pulse oximetry: Millikan (1942) and Wood & Geraci's (1949) pneumatic bloodless-ear zeroing, Takuo Aoyagi's (1974) breakthrough using pulsatile arterial AC/DC absorbance ratios at two wavelengths, two-wavelength degrees-of-freedom failure in carboxyhemoglobinemia and methemoglobinemia, and melanin/low-saturation occult hypoxemia bias (Bickler et al. 2005; Sjoding et al. 2020).

item.title: How an Electrode Learned to Measure Glucose — Clark & Lyons's 1962 Enzyme Membrane Electrode, Updike & Hicks's 1967 Dual-Cathode Differential Sensor & Basu's 2013 Interstitial Lag
item.description: Electrochemical and physiological foundations of continuous glucose monitoring (CGM): Clark & Lyons's (1962) enzyme-membrane electrode concept, Updike & Hicks's (1967) dual-cathode active-vs-inactivated polyacrylamide 'enzyme electrode' canceling ambient oxygen drift, subcutaneous interstitial fluid sensing and electroactive drug interference, and Basu et al.'s (2013) human tracer microdialysis proof of physiological capillary-to-interstitial glucose lag.

Traces the polymorphic CYP2D6 ultra-rapid metabolism and neonatal blood-brain barrier kinetics that converted standard postpartum analgesia into a lethal dose via breast milk transfer.

Examines how unconjugated drug accumulation inhibits mitochondrial protein synthesis, triggering hypothermia, cyanosis, and fatal cardiovascular gray baby collapse.
item.itunes:summary: Pharmacokinetic and toxicological dissection of neonatal chloramphenicol toxicity and hepatic UGT2B7 glucuronidation immaturity. item.title: How Henna Caused Newborn Brain Damage
item.itunes:title: How Henna Caused Newborn Brain Damage

Analyzes the vulnerability of the porous neonatal blood-brain barrier and dormant hepatic enzymes to lawsone-induced oxidative stress and hyperbilirubinemia within a cultural and clinical framework.

item.description: Toxicological and pharmacogenetic audit of metamizole-induced agranulocytosis. Analyzes the bone marrow immune suppression mechanisms, reactive metabolite pathways, and international regulatory discrepancies surrounding dipyrone withdrawal.
item.itunes:summary: Toxicological and pharmacogenetic audit of metamizole-induced agranulocytosis. Analyzes the bone marrow immune suppression mechanisms, reactive metabolite pathways, and international regulatory discrepancies surrounding dipyrone withdrawal.

item.title: Why Germany Prescribes America's Banned Painkiller
item.itunes:title: Why Germany Prescribes America's Banned Painkiller
item.itunes:author: Matthew S. Yorek
item.description: Comparative pharmacological and regulatory audit of metamizole, a non-opioid analgesic banned by the FDA in 1977 yet widely utilized in German clinical practice. Evaluates the idiosyncratic risk of agranulocytosis against the drug’s efficacy profile, highlighting international discrepancies in hematologic safety thresholds and risk-benefit calculus.
item.itunes:summary: Comparative pharmacological and regulatory audit of metamizole, a non-opioid analgesic banned by the FDA in 1977 yet widely utilized in German clinical practice. Evaluates the idiosyncratic risk of agranulocytosis against the drug’s efficacy profile, highlighting international discrepancies in hematologic safety thresholds and risk-benefit calculus.

item.title: How Licorice Tea Caused Sudden Paralysis
item.itunes:title: How Licorice Tea Caused Sudden Paralysis
item.itunes:author: Matthew S. Yorek
item.description: Clinical and toxicological dissection of pseudohyperaldosteronism induced by excessive glycyrrhizic acid intake from licorice tea. Traces the molecular disruption of electrolyte homeostasis that precipitates sudden flaccid paralysis, hypertensive crisis, and imminent cardiac arrest through the inhibition of 11β-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase type 2.
item.itunes:summary: Clinical and toxicological dissection of pseudohyperaldosteronism induced by excessive glycyrrhizic acid intake from licorice tea. Traces the molecular disruption of electrolyte homeostasis that precipitates sudden flaccid paralysis, hypertensive crisis, and imminent cardiac arrest through the inhibition of 11β-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase type 2.

item.title: How Soviet Mint Drops Triggered Seizures
item.itunes:title: How Soviet Mint Drops Triggered Seizures
item.itunes:author: Matthew S. Yorek
item.description: Clinical and neuropharmacological dissection of covert barbiturate withdrawal seizures triggered by abrupt discontinuation of Soviet peppermint drops (Corvalol) alongside porcine Cerebrolysin therapy. Traces hidden phenobarbital and ethyl bromoisovalerate GABA-A receptor dependence behind iatrogenic status epilepticus.
item.itunes:summary: Clinical and neuropharmacological dissection of covert barbiturate withdrawal seizures triggered by abrupt discontinuation of Soviet peppermint drops (Corvalol) alongside porcine Cerebrolysin therapy. item.title: How Amphetamines Killed Tom Simpson
item.itunes:title: How Amphetamines Killed Tom Simpson
item.itunes:author: Matthew S. Yorek
item.description: Clinical and forensic reconstruction of the fatal intersection between amphetamine use and the evolutionary circuit breaker of physical exhaustion during extreme athletic exertion. Traces the pharmacodynamic suppression of vital fatigue signals that led to the collapse of Tom Simpson by overriding homeostatic limits and metabolic safeguards.
item.itunes:summary: Clinical and forensic reconstruction of the fatal intersection between amphetamine use and the evolutionary circuit breaker of physical exhaustion during extreme athletic exertion. item.title: Gill Lamellae, Trunk Kidneys, Exhaust Dust, and Brainstems — Teleost Gill Wet Mounts & Gas Bubble Disease (V053), Aquatic Kidney Culture, 37°C Traps & FDA VFDs (V054), Lab Rodent Exhaust Air Dust PCR (V055) & Wildlife Rabies DFA & CDC LN34 RT-qPCR (V056)
item.description: One Medicine Capstone synthesis of teleost wet mounts (V053), fish bacteriology (V054), lab rodent surveillance (V055), and wildlife rabies testing (V056): 15m gill autolysis clock, buffered MS-222, Gyrodactylus vs. Dactylogyrus, and Gas Bubble Disease; Posterior Trunk Kidney culture, 15-28C thermal/TYES media, CLSI VET03/04, and FDA VFD law; IVC Exhaust Air Dust qPCR, NSG serology traps, binomial n=299 math, and LCMV biologics PCR; and bilateral Brainstem+Cerebellum DFA, CDC LN34 decomposed-brain rescue, cryptic bedroom bats, and FAVN titers.

item.title: The Number After the Blood Was Cleared — Pre-Dialysis Lithium Rebound, 7Li Brain MRS Half-Life, Spent-Tank Dialysate Recovery & EXTRIP Cohort Predictions
item.description: Multi-compartment pharmacokinetics and clinical toxicology of lithium clearance: pre-dialysis serum rebound during IV hydration in chronic toxicity with nephrogenic diabetes insipidus (Kobylianskii et al. 2021, 1.50->0.40->1.30 mmol/L), human 7Li brain magnetic resonance spectroscopy vs. serum half-lives (Plenge et al. 1994), direct mass recovery of 250 mg lithium in collected spent dialysate vs. serum percentage reduction (Schmidt et al. 2014), and retrospective evaluation of EXTRIP dialysis criteria across 361 poisonings (Buckley et al. 2020).

item.title: The Level That Rose After the Last Pill — Delayed Enteric & Modified-Release Absorption, Pharmacobezoars, Auto-Inhibition & Rising Post-Admission Drug Levels
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology investigation of rising post-ingestion drug concentrations in hospitalized patients: modified-release formulation kinetics, pyloric spasm and ileus, pharmacobezoar formation, and why a single triage drug level misses late peak toxicity.

item.title: What the Hair Could Tell Us — Early Iron Age Tunnug 1 Cannabis Burial, Hair-Shaft CBN LC-HRMS/MS vs. Environmental Transfer, Human CB1-Gi1 Cryo-EM (PDB 9ERX) & Hallstatt Radiocarbon
item.description: Archaeotoxicology and receptor pharmacology of ancient cannabis at Tunnug 1 (Tuva, Early Iron Age): LC-HRMS/MS detection of cannabinol (CBN) in a preserved human hair braid alongside 965 botanical cannabis seeds, Hallstatt Plateau 14C calibration, human CB1-Gi1 cryo-EM structure (PDB 9ERX), forensic hair-testing boundaries between smoke/handling transfer and metabolic THC-COOH incorporation (Moosmann et al. 2015), and comparative Eurasian archaeobotany.

item.title: The Aspirin That Changed the Breathing — Hoffmann's Acetylsalicylic Acid, Vane's Prostaglandin Blockade & Human COX-2 Ser530 Acetylation (5F19 vs. 5F1A), Mitochondrial Uncoupling, Chloride Electrode Artifacts & EXTRIP Dialysis
item.description: Covalent enzyme acetylation meets clinical toxicology: Hoffmann's 1900 aspirin patent, Vane and Smith & Willis's 1971 prostaglandin inhibition, Roth's irreversible platelet COX acetylation, and Lucido's human COX-2 crystal structures (acetylated Ser530 in PDB 5F19 vs. salicylate-bound 5F1A), paired with a serial salicylate poisoning timeline showing mixed respiratory alkalosis and high-anion-gap acidosis, salicylate-induced chloride ISE pseudohyperchloremia, mitochondrial protonophoric uncoupling, pH-dependent nonionized CNS entry, and EXTRIP hemodialysis criteria.

item.title: Lithium and the Level That Came Back — Cade & Schou, Lithium-Heparin Tube Artifacts, GSK-3β Mg2+ Competition, ENaC Nephrogenic DI & Post-Dialysis Rebound
item.description: Clinical and molecular dissection of lithium toxicity: lithium-heparin green-top collection tube false elevations (Wills et al.), GSK-3β and IMPase Mg2+ competition (PDB 1PYX, 2BJI), collecting-duct ENaC entry (PDB 6BQN) and AQP2 downregulation, and EXTRIP hemodialysis rebound kinetics.

item.title: Foxglove, Digoxin & the Number That Rose After Rescue — Withering's Dropsy, Na+/K+-ATPase 4RET, DigiFab Immunoassay Interference & Free vs. Total LC-MS/MS
item.description: From William Withering's 1785 dropsy cases to the 4 A porcine Na+/K+-ATPase crystal structure (4RET), UHPLC-MS/MS MRM transitions, and why ovine DigiFab rescue causes total serum digoxin immunoassays to surge twelvefold while free pharmacologically active digoxin plummets.

item.title: The Number After the Sting — Postmortem Tryptase Site Divergence (8,955 Antemortem vs. <5,000 Central vs. 319 Peripheral ng/mL), Systemic Mastocytosis Baselines & Anaphylaxis Thresholds
item.description: Forensic pathology and clinical toxicology of fatal insect-sting anaphylaxis: dramatic divergence between antemortem catheter blood (8,955 ng/mL), postmortem central blood (<5,000 ng/mL), and postmortem peripheral femoral blood (319 ng/mL), systemic mastocytosis baseline tryptase elevation, and why isolated postmortem cutoffs fail without anatomic sampling discipline.

item.title: The Lunch That Looked Like an Allergy — Scombroid Histamine Fish Poisoning, Paris Yellowfin Tuna Outbreak (40 Cases, 39/79 Attack Rate), Heat-Stable Histidine Decarboxylation & Supply-Chain Forensics
item.description: Outbreak epidemiology and food toxicology of scombroid histamine fish poisoning: Velut et al.'s (2019) Paris military-canteen yellowfin tuna outbreak (40 cases, 39/79 tuna diners vs. 31-case/63-control questionnaire), bacterial histidine decarboxylation into heat-stable histamine mimicking IgE anaphylaxis, CDC 2006 Louisiana/Tennessee tuna traceback contrasts, and FDA CPG 540.525 surveillance rules.

item.title: The Lactate That Wasn't There — Ethylene Glycol Poisoning, Point-of-Care Glycolate Oxidase Cross-Reactivity & True Lab Lactate
item.description: Behind the Curtain forensic & clinical toxicology analysis of ethylene glycol poisoning: why blood-gas point-of-care L-lactate oxidase electrodes misread glycolate as massive hyperlactatemia while core-lab assays reveal the true lactate gap (Hauvik et al. 2018).

item.title: What the Bottle Could Not Tell — Postmortem Toxicology Redistribution, Pill-Bottle Scene Priors vs. Femoral Blood Quantification & Tolerance Boundaries
item.description: Forensic toxicology investigation of why pill bottles and scene containers cannot establish cause of death alone: postmortem central-to-peripheral redistribution, femoral vs. cardiac blood sampling, quantitative LC-MS/MS confirmation, and acquired opioid/sedative tolerance.

item.title: The Alarm Beyond the Wall — Post-Storm Portable Generator Exhaust Aerodynamics (167 Florida Cases, 16 Outdoor vs. 16 Garage), Wind-Wake Infiltration, Pulse Oximetry SpO2 Blindness & Battery CO Alarms
item.description: Forensic investigation of post-storm portable generator carbon monoxide infiltration: 2004 Florida hurricane hospital/CPSC records (167 nonfatal cases in 51 incidents; 16 outdoor vs. 16 garage generators), aerodynamic wake infiltration through windows and window AC units, two-wavelength pulse oximetry SpO2 optical blindness vs. CO-oximetry, and North Carolina ice-storm battery-backed CO alarm survival evidence.

item.title: The Drug Behind the Result — Lisdexamfetamine Prodrugs, Chiral d/l-Amphetamine LC-MS/MS & Matrix Stability
item.description: Behind the Curtain Evidence Ledger & Longform Analysis (The Drug Behind the Result): specimen-bound diagnostic mechanics, assay boundaries, and real clinical/forensic case studies.

item.title: One Ångström from a Dividing Cell — Paclitaxel in the β-Tubulin Taxane Pocket (1JFF), Cremophor Anaphylaxis & Mitotic Spindle Fate
item.description: Atomic-scale journey into the luminal beta-tubulin taxane pocket (PDB 1JFF): distinguishing Cremophor EL complement-mediated infusion anaphylaxis from delayed neutropenia, M-loop lateral protofilament stabilization, and multipolar mitotic spindle catastrophe in human tumors.

item.title: The Antibody and the Unhealed Colon — Infliximab TNF-Alpha Trimer Crystal Structure (PDB 4G3Y), Transmembrane Avidity, Endoscopic Mucosal Healing (ACT 1/2) & Anti-Drug Antibody Clearance
item.description: Structural immunology and therapeutic drug monitoring of infliximab in ulcerative colitis: chimeric cA2 engineering (Knight 1993), 2.60 Å TNF-alpha:infliximab Fab crystal structure (PDB 4G3Y, Liang 2013), transmembrane TNF bivalent avidity (Scallon 2002), ACT 1 & ACT 2 mucosal healing trials (Rutgeerts 2005), and anti-drug antibody clearance vs. assay non-interchangeability.

item.title: The Drug That Took the Long Way — Parkinson's Vallecular Tablet Retention on Videofluoroscopy, Enterococcus faecalis TyrDC Gut Decarboxylation & Oral vs. Jejunal Levodopa-Carbidopa Gel Kinetics
item.description: Mechanical and microbial bottlenecks along levodopa's route from mouth to brain: videofluoroscopic discovery of tablet retention in the valleculae (Sato et al. 2018), carbidopa-insensitive gut microbial tyrosine decarboxylase (Enterococcus faecalis TyrDC) and Eggerthella lenta dopamine dehydroxylase (Maini Rekdal et al. 2019; van Kessel et al. 2019), and oral vs. continuous jejunal infusion pharmacokinetics (Othman et al. 2015).

item.title: The Breath Before the Heat — Rising End-Tidal CO2 Before Hyperthermia, Skeletal Muscle RyR1 Calcium Leak, Dantrolene Channel Stabilization & Post-Crisis IVCT/CHCT vs. RYR1 Genetic Testing
item.description: Intraoperative malignant hyperthermia from capnography to channel biophysics: why rising end-tidal carbon dioxide precedes core temperature elevation, uncontrolled skeletal muscle ryanodine receptor (RyR1) sarcoplasmic reticulum calcium release, dantrolene sodium stabilization of RyR1, and post-crisis workup integrating RYR1 variant sequencing with caffeine-halothane contracture testing.

item.title: The Channel That Wouldn't Let Calcium Through — Extended-Release Verapamil Overdose, Fleckenstein's Calcium Antagonism, Rabbit CaV1.1 Cryo-EM (6JPA), Beta-Cell Hyperglycemia & High-Dose Insulin Therapy
item.description: From Albrecht Fleckenstein's discovery of calcium antagonism to critical-care toxicology: rabbit CaV1.1 cryo-EM structure bound to (S)-verapamil in two central-cavity poses (PDB 6JPA), AV-nodal conduction block, pancreatic beta-cell L-type channel blockade producing diagnostic hyperglycemia, stereoselective CYP3A4 clearance, high-dose insulin euglycemia therapy, and EXTRIP non-dialyzability.

item.title: The Sedative the Screen Missed — GABAA alpha1-beta2-gamma2 Cryo-EM Allosteric Binding (6X3X/6X3U), Diazepam CYP2C19/3A4 vs. Lorazepam Direct UGT2B15 Glucuronidation & Why Urine Immunoassays Miss Lorazepam-Glucuronide
item.description: Receptor allostery, metabolic routing, and toxicology screen blind spots: cryo-EM structures of human alpha1-beta2-gamma2 GABAA receptors bound to diazepam (PDB 6X3X) and flumazenil (PDB 6X3U), Sternbach's benzodiazepine chemistry, diazepam CYP oxidation vs. lorazepam direct C3-OH glucuronidation, and why unhydrolyzed urine benzodiazepine immunoassays miss lorazepam-glucuronide without beta-glucuronidase hydrolysis and LC-MS/MS.

item.title: The Dose That Bought Another Hour — Parkinson's Levodopa Wearing-Off Diaries, Catechol-O-Methyltransferase (COMT) Mg2+ Coordination (PDB 7XGI), Opicapone Erythrocyte Kinetics, BIPARK-I & Tolcapone Hepatotoxicity
item.description: From Parkinson's wearing-off diaries to peripheral COMT inhibition: separating seated motor OFF time from orthostatic hypotension, competing AADC and COMT metabolic pathways, rat soluble COMT crystal structure bound to opicapone and Mg2+ (PDB 7XGI), plasma LC-MS/MS vs. sustained erythrocyte COMT inhibition kinetics, BIPARK-I/II trial endpoints, and tolcapone vs. opicapone hepatic safety.

item.title: The Dose the Liver Had to Finish — Clopidogrel Thienopyridine Prodrug Bioactivation, CYP2C19 Loss-of-Function Alleles, Rapid GMEX Genotyping & the CHANCE-2 Trial
item.description: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology investigation of clopidogrel (Plavix) hepatic two-step CYP2C19 bioactivation vs. CES1 esterase hydrolysis: why CYP2C19*2/*3 loss-of-function alleles leave platelets uninhibited, point-of-care GMEX genotyping validation, CPIC clinical guidelines, and the CHANCE-2 ticagrelor-vs.-clopidogrel stroke trial.

item.title: Half-Lives, Pancreatic Epitopes, and Portal Shunts — Human Therapeutic Drug Monitoring, Vancomycin AUC24 & Winter-Tozer/DigiFab Traps (H056), Canine/Feline Monoclonal Spec cPL/fPL & Triaditis (V025) & Dynamic Paired Bile Acids, Maltese Artifacts & PSS vs. MVD (V026)
item.description: One Medicine synthesis of human therapeutic drug monitoring (H056), canine/feline pancreatic lipase (V025), and dynamic serum bile acid stimulation (V026): phenytoin zero-order kinetics & Winter-Tozer free fraction, digoxin 6-8h & post-DigiFab traps, Bayesian vancomycin AUC24/MIC, and EDTA whole-blood tacrolimus LC-MS/MS; Spec cPL/fPL vs. catalytic lipase failure, feline shared-ampulla Triaditis + B12, cTLI for EPI, and foreign-body bystander cPL; and 12h/2h bile acids, the jaundice ban, Maltese chromogens, and Protein C (<70% PSS vs. >=70% benign MVD).

item.title: The Potassium That Rose in the Tube — Reverse Pseudohyperkalemia in Leukocytosis, Pneumatic Tube Shear vs. Hand-Carried Whole Blood, Cold-Induced ABCB6 Leak & ECG Sensitivity Traps
item.description: Dissecting in-vitro potassium artifacts before the analyzer: Mansoor et al. (2015) reverse pseudohyperkalemia (9.5 mmol/L across three analyzers vs. 3.7 mmol/L on hand-carried whole blood due to pneumatic-tube mechanical lysis of fragile leukemic white cells in heparinized plasma), Xiong et al. (2022) familial cold-induced ABCB6 red-cell potassium leak, and Raffee et al. (2022) why a normal ECG cannot rule out true hyperkalemia.

item.title: Alkaline Lithium Springs & Unchained Asylums — Soranus of Ephesus & Humane Roman Psychiatry
item.description: How Soranus of Ephesus (~100 CE) condemned chains, darkness, and the 'wandering womb' myth while prescribing cognitive rehabilitation and lithium-rich alkaline waters.

item.title: Where Does Pain Actually Live? — Anzio Beachhead, Nav1.7 & Predictive Interoception
item.description: Debates peripheral nociceptive specificity (Nav1.7 SCN9A) vs. top-down insular predictive interoception (Beecher at Anzio, 1995 boot-nail case, naloxone placebo blockade).
